blocks.prompt: 5 A giant Ferris wheel has a diameter of 60 feet. The lowest point of the wheel is located 6 feet above the ground. The wheel completes one full revolution every 80 seconds. (a) Model an equation that represent the height \(h(t)\) of a rider on the Ferris wheel at any given time \(t\).
blocks.explanation:
A modelling question: build \(h(t) = a + b\cos(ct)\) from the facts.
We need the centre height, the radius and \(c\).
Plan: radius \(=\) half the diameter; centre \(=\) lowest point \(+\) radius; \(c = \frac{2\pi}{\text{period}}\); start at the bottom.
steps:
Given: diameter 60 ft, lowest point 6 ft above the ground, one revolution in 80 s.
To find: a formula for \(h(t)\).
Method: Height on a turning wheel \(= \text{centre} \pm \text{radius} \times \cos(\ldots)\). We take \(t = 0\) when the rider gets on at the lowest point (the usual assumption; the question does not say), so we use \(-\cos\), which starts at its lowest value.

Radius (amplitude)
\[r = \tfrac{60}{2} = 30 \text{ ft}\]
Why: The rider goes 30 ft above and 30 ft below the centre.

Height of the centre (midline)
\[a = 6 + 30 = 36 \text{ ft}\]
Why: The lowest point is one radius below the centre.

Angular speed \(c\)
\[c = \dfrac{2\pi}{80} = \dfrac{\pi}{40}\]
Why: One revolution is \(2\pi\) radians in 80 s, so \(\frac{2\pi}{c} = 80\).

Write the model
\[h(t) = 36 - 30\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{40}t\right)\]
Why: At \(t = 0\), \(\cos 0 = 1\) gives \(36 - 30 = 6\): the rider starts at the lowest point.

Check
\[h(0) = 36 - 30 = 6 \;\checkmark\]
\[h(40) = 36 - 30\cos\pi = 66 \;\checkmark\]
\[h(80) = 6 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Lowest at the start, highest after half a turn, back at the bottom after one full turn (80 s).

blocks.prompt: 5 A giant Ferris wheel has a diameter of 60 feet. The lowest point of the wheel is located 6 feet above the ground. The wheel completes one full revolution every 80 seconds. (b) Find the maximum height of a rider.
blocks.explanation:
The highest point of the wheel.
We need the largest value of \(h(t)\).
Plan: use \(-1 \le \cos \le 1\) in the model.
steps:
Given: \(h(t) = 36 - 30\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{40}t\right)\).
To find: the maximum of \(h\).
Method: Cosine lies between \(-1\) and \(1\); the minus sign makes \(h\) largest when cosine is \(-1\).

Range of the cosine part
\[-1 \le \cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{40}t\right) \le 1\]
\[30 \ge -30\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{40}t\right) \ge -30\]
Why: Multiplying by \(-30\) reverses the signs.

Add 36
\[66 \ge h(t) \ge 6\]
Why: 36 is the centre height.

Check
\[h(40) = 36 - 30(-1) = 66\]
\[\text{Top} = 6 + 60 = 66 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Lowest point plus the diameter gives the same top height.

blocks.prompt: 5 A giant Ferris wheel has a diameter of 60 feet. The lowest point of the wheel is located 6 feet above the ground. The wheel completes one full revolution every 80 seconds. (c) Find the height of the rider from the ground after 35 seconds.
blocks.explanation:
Substitution into the model from part (a).
We need \(h(35)\).
Plan: work out the angle \(\frac{35\pi}{40}\), its cosine, then \(h\).
steps:
Given: \(h(t) = 36 - 30\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{40}t\right)\), \(t = 35\).
To find: \(h(35)\).
Method: Substitute; \(\frac{7\pi}{8} = 157.5^{\circ}\) is in Quadrant II, where cosine is negative.

Find \(h\)
\[h(35) = 36 - 30(-0.92388)\]
\[= 36 + 27.716\]
\[\approx 63.72 \text{ ft}\]
Why: Minus a negative is a plus.

Check
\[6 \le 63.72 \le 66 \;\checkmark\]
Why: 35 s is just before the top (40 s), so the rider should be a little below 66 ft, and is.
